  "content": "---\nid: moka-pot-grasp-the-handle-not-the-body\nscope: global\nkind: strategy\ntitle: Grasp a moka pot by its thin side handle, not its wide body or cap\napplies_when: picking a moka pot (or any wide low-poly pot/kettle with a slim handle)\n  when top-down body grasps stall and Pi0 will not close\nsymptom:\n- moka pot\n- pi0 never closes\n- gripper opening 0.078\n- descent stalls on shoulder\n- cap grasp slips\n- wide body grasp\nevidence:\n  cells:\n  - 10_task_t8_s0\n  attempts: 3\n  solved_seeds:\n  - 0\nconfidence: single-shot\nrelated: []\n---\n\nA moka pot is reliably grasped top-down by its thin side HANDLE; its wide octagonal body and thin cap knob are both un-graspable and Pi0 refuses to close on it.\n\n**Why:** The pot's upper chamber/shoulder is ~7.8cm across \u2014 essentially the gripper's full open span (~8cm) \u2014 so open fingers collide with the shoulder and the OSC descent stalls before the fingers can straddle the body; the only narrow top-down feature (the cap knob, ~1cm) gives a gap-0.012 pinch that slips. The handle is a slim (~1.5-2cm) rigid tube offset laterally from the body, so fingers descend around it without shoulder collision and close to a firm gap ~0.020. Pi0 (pi0_pick) descended but never issued a close command on this pot in 3/3 tries \u2014 its trained distribution does not commit to this geometry.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- Localize the handle's top-of-curve segment (back_project pixels). Note the tube axis; rotate the\n  wrist yaw ~90deg so the fingers close ACROSS the tube (not along it). A 90deg rotate_wrist drifts\n  the eef ~0.1-0.15m \u2014 re-center over the handle before descending.\n- Descend to tube level (~z where finger tips meet the tube), set_gripper +1.   "size": 2053,
  "content": "---\nid: libero-in-predicate-fires-while-grasped\nscope: global\nkind: strategy\ntitle: Test placement targets by holding the object over them and watching libero_terminated,\n  before releasing\napplies_when: an In()/On() place task where the correct destination among several\n  look-alikes is uncertain, or where releasing risks tipping/losing the object\nsymptom:\n- wrong compartment\n- which container\n- ambiguous target\n- place predicate not firing\n- cannot re-grasp\n- tipped after release\n- in predicate\nevidence:\n  cells:\n  - 10_task_t5_s0\n  attempts: 4\n  solved_seeds:\n  - 0\nconfidence: single-shot\nrelated:\n- caddy-back-is-near-robot-pocket\n---\n\n\nLIBERO In()/On() success predicates check the OBJECT'S POSE, not the gripper\nstate, so `libero_terminated` flips the moment the held object's pose satisfies\nthe region \u2014 you do NOT have to release first.\n\n**Why:** libero_terminated mirrors the BDDL goal predicate, which is a function\nof object poses only. Releasing is irrelevant to the check (confirmed: placing a\nmug in the correct caddy pocket fired while still grasped; placing/releasing in\nthree WRONG pockets never fired).\n**How to apply:**\n- To disambiguate among candidate destinations, carry the still-grasped object\n  (gripper +1) low over each candidate and read `libero_terminated` from the\n  returned state. Move to the next candidate if it stays false \u2014 no release, no\n  re-grasp, no commitment. This turns an N-way target guess into N cheap probes.\n- Only `release` after the flag is already true (or to seat a confirmed target).\n- Corollary: a non-firing predicate with a clean, low, upright placement is\n  evidence of WRONG DESTINATION, not wrong physics \u2014 switch targets first.\n- Caveat: some tasks pair In() with a \"not in gripper\"/stack-stability term; if a\n  held probe won't fire but the geometry looks perfect, release once to check.\n**Falsify:** a place task where the predicate provably requires the gripper open\n(object released) and a correctly-posed held object does NOT fire.\n**Related:** [[caddy-back-is-near-robot-pocket]]\n"
}

  "content": "---\nid: rotate-wrist-90deg-drifts-eef-recenter-after\nscope: global\nkind: primitive\ntitle: A large rotate_wrist yaw drifts the eef ~0.1-0.15m; re-center before descending\napplies_when: you rotate_wrist by a large yaw (e.g. 90deg) to align fingers, then\n  need a precise xy over a target\nsymptom:\n- rotate_wrist moved eef\n- yaw rotation drift\n- gripper off target after yaw\n- position changed after rotate_wrist\nevidence:\n  cells:\n  - 10_task_t8_s0\n  attempts: 1\n  solved_seeds:\n  - 0\nconfidence: single-shot\nrelated:\n- moka-pot-grasp-the-handle-not-the-body\n---\n\nAlthough rotate_wrist is documented to hold xyz fixed, a large yaw change (~90deg) can move the eef by ~0.1-0.15m in xy; always re-issue a move_to to the target after the rotation and before descending.\n\n**Why:** observed, cause likely OSC/IK: holding eef position while commanding a big wrist reorientation drives the arm through a configuration where the position controller cannot fully compensate, so the eef settles offset. (Mechanism not verified beyond the observation.)\n\n**How to apply:**\n- Order operations as: rotate_wrist to the needed yaw FIRST (accept the drift), THEN move_to the\n  precise xy target, THEN descend. Do not descend immediately after a large rotate_wrist.\n- Budget one extra move_to. Small yaw tweaks (<~20deg) drift much less and may not need it.\n\n**Falsify:** If large rotate_wrist yaw changes on other cells leave the eef within ~1cm of its\npre-rotation xy, the drift is scene-specific and this can be narrowed.\n\n**Related:** [[moka-pot-grasp-the-handle-not-the-body]]\n"
}
